context_requirements: No annotated molecular targets are listed for this class in the Drug Repurposing Hub, so no host-cell transcriptional program can be predicted.
Antiviral/antiparasitic antiinfectives act on pathogen enzymes or processes (e.g., artesunate on Plasmodium/herpesvirus factors) that are absent in uninfected human cell lines.
A transcriptional response would require active infection or a host target; these nine lines are cultured uninfected cells.
Any observed changes would most likely reflect nonspecific cytotoxicity at 10 micromolar rather than the antiinfective mechanism.
falsifiers: A reproducible, dose-dependent and cell-line-selective transcriptional signature at 6 h that is shared across chemically unrelated antiinfectives and absent for non-antiinfective drugs.
Evidence that a specific host target of this class is expressed and engaged in these lines (e.g., rescue by target overexpression or knockdown).
Clear separation of responsive versus non-responsive lines by expression of a defined host receptor or enzyme rather than by general drug sensitivity.

evidence.supports: Artesunate, a broad-spectrum antiinfective, inhibits herpesvirus protein synthesis and genome replication in cultured human cells without drug-induced apoptosis or necrosis, indicating the antiviral effect is pathogen-directed rather than a host transcriptional program.
